chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Abu al-Subbah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and found a 'horn' in her. He said: 'This one does not get pregnant, and her husband cannot have intercourse with her; he returns her to her family humiliated and she has no dowry.' I said: 'But if he had intercourse with her?' He said: 'If he knew of that before marrying her, meaning intercourse, then he married her, he has accepted her. And if he did not know until after he had intercourse with her, then if he wishes he keeps her, and if he wishes he divorces her.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And when a man marries a woman on the basis that she is a virgin and finds her to be non-virgin, he does not have the right to return her. That is indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.قَرْناً: A physical defect or mark, often referring to the hymen or a specific anatomical feature, used here to denote virginity status or fertility

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband discovers his wife has a physical defect preventing intercourse after marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudence of *Gharar* (uncertainty) in marriage by distinguishing between defects that nullify the purpose of marriage (preventing intercourse) and those that do not. It establishes that if the defect prevents consummation, the wife is returned without a dowry; if consummation occurred, the husband retains the option to keep or divorce her. Additionally, it notes that marrying for virginity does not grant the right to return the wife if she turns out to be non-virginal, emphasizing the stability of the marital bond.
